newsitem.title: UK: De Beers sees scope for higher sales.
newsitem.headline: De Beers sees scope for higher sales.

text.p: De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd said on Tuesday it expected its production and sales of rough diamonds to grow as Russia's stockpile decreases.
With fewer Russian diamonds expected to directly come on to world markets, De Beers should benefit from jewellery demand growing in line with economies worldwide.
"As Russian stocks are sold down there should be scope for increased group production and group sales," De Beers said in its 1996 annual report.
Sales of the South African company, which has its marketing organisation based in London, rose seven percent to a record $4.83 billion in 1996.
De Beers, which controls about 75 percent of world trade in uncut diamonds, in March reported 1996 attributable earnings rose to $828 million from $624 million.
The company is still awaiting a Russian decision on a crucial marketing deal with the country's largest diamond producer.
A draft agreement was signed in September, but the deal still needs Russia's official approval.
Diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha said earlier Russia would decide on April 15, but no news emerged.
De Beers, showing frustration at the time it was taking to reach a decision, stopped buying stones from Russia under a previous agreement at the end of last year.
